# AI usage log

## Disclosure (please read first)
**Most of this repository - code, tests, documents and this log's first draft - was generated by Claude (Anthropic) in one working
session at the candidate's request** (the candidate asked for the whole project to be built, packaged and explained). Claude ran the code
in a sandbox (offline tests, offline evaluation, a local server smoke test). Claude had **no API key and no network access to an LLM
provider**, so the live LLM path (`PROVIDER=openai_compat`) has only been tested with mocked HTTP.

> **Candidate to complete before submitting:** what you personally read, ran, changed and verified (e.g. ran `make test`, ran
> `make eval-live` with your Gemini key, edits you made), and any other AI tools you used. This must be true; you will be asked to
> explain and modify any part of the code live.

## Tools
Claude (Anthropic) via claude.ai with code execution (sandbox: Python 3.12, pdfplumber, FastAPI, pytest).

## Key prompts (actual)
1. Candidate's request: accept the assignment, make the whole project professional and complete, give a zip, explain how to run it on the laptop, push to GitHub, record the video and submit (message in the chat, written in Hinglish, with the invitation email and the zip).
2. Claude's own working steps (not separate user prompts): inspect the pack; diff old vs update PDFs to discover what changed (SOP-02, 08, 11 content; SOP-05 renamed; SOP-15 withdrawn; SOP-16, 17 new); design; implement; run tests/eval; write docs.
3. Design-proposal prompt: see `docs/ai_design_proposal.md` (prompt saved there).

*(Add your own follow-up prompts here if you continue the work in another session.)*

## Places where the AI was wrong or weak, and how it was caught
| # | What went wrong | How it was caught | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Refusal gate wrongly refused answerable questions: U01 ("percentage" vs "25%" in the PDF) and Q04 ("fridge" vs "refrigerator") | Running the evaluation and reading per-question output, not just the pass count | Text normalisation (`%`->percent, small synonym list), then wrote a **held-out** paraphrase set because tuning on the eval questions inflates results; remaining 2/12 false refusals are documented, not hidden |
| 2 | First ingestion report listed 11 documents as "renamed" | Reading the ingest log of the update run - only SOP-05 was really renamed; the AI compared full paths (folder changed) not file names | Separate "moved" (silent metadata update) from "renamed" (reported); test asserts SOP-05 only |
| 3 | First fake LLM cited irrelevant chunks, making citation checks meaningless, and an offline pass could be mistaken for answer quality | Looking at citation lists in the smoke output (Q06 cited an HR SOP for a refund question) | Redefined the fake as an explicit "echo" of retrieved context and labelled offline eval as retrieval/plumbing only; eval report and README say so |
| 4 | Shell command with `{a,b,c}` brace expansion ran under `sh` and created a directory literally named `{domain,adapters,...}`; first parser draft also contained a convoluted `is_table` heuristic that did nothing | `ls` / `find` after the command; reading the parser diff | Removed the directory, rewrote the structure, deleted the dead code |
| 5 | Test speed-up used `lru_cache` on a function taking an unhashable frozen dataclass: 40 tests errored | Test run | Replaced with a plain dict keyed by path |
| 6 | The design proposal itself (see `design_review.md`) had real flaws: file-name identity, non-atomic reindex, semantic cache without role key, LLM-based PII | Checked against the actual pack (SOP-05 rename, SOP-11 v1.2 vs v2.0, role-restricted SOP-13/17) | Overruled in ADR-1/2/3 |

## What I would still verify by hand
Live-model behaviour (answer wording, `NOT_COVERED` compliance, conflict handling), gate thresholds with a real embedder, the Gemini model/embedding names and prices, and the PDF parser on real (not synthetic) SOPs.
